title: Marvel's 'Wonder Man' Show Canceled—Even Though Everyone Was Ready to Go!
summary: Imagine you're all set to start a big, exciting project—then suddenly, it's canceled. That's what happened to the team behind Marvel's 'Wonder Man.' The show's co-creator, Andrew Guest, made a TikTok video to share his feelings. He said this isn't a trick or a marketing stunt. 'Contracts were signed, schedules were cleared,' he explained. The writers were supposed to start this month, and filming was set for early next year. But Disney and Marvel decided not to continue. Guest said he, the director Destin Daniel Cretton, and the star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II all loved making the show and wanted to keep going. Yahya even won an Emmy for his role as Simon Williams, a superhero who is also an actor. He posted on Instagram, 'That's life, right? Everything will shake out.' The show was about Simon trying to land a role in a superhero movie remake, with help from an older actor played by Sir Ben Kingsley. Fans are disappointed, but Guest wanted them to know the truth. Sometimes, even when everyone is ready and excited, plans change.
why_it_matters: Sometimes, even when you work hard and prepare everything, plans can change unexpectedly—and that's okay, just like when a school project gets rescheduled.

background_read: Wonder Man is a superhero from Marvel Comics first created in 1964; he started as a villain but later became a hero.
The show was supposed to be part of Disney+ (the Walt Disney Company's streaming service) where Marvel has made hits like 'WandaVision' and 'Loki'.
Yahya Abdul-Mateen II (the actor who previously won an Emmy for his role in 'Watchmen') was excited to play the lead, but the project was stopped before filming could begin.
